jurisdiction.name: Andorra
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Andorra governs AI mainly through the government's May 2024 Code on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence and two 2024 decrees creating a Data Intelligence Agency, with AI supervision functions, and a Data Intelligence Office in the administration. Its GDPR-style personal data protection law (Law 29/2021) regulates automated decisions, and the new Criminal Code published in August 2026 makes AI-generated sexual deepfakes an offence from December 2026. Andorra has no AI law or published national AI strategy, and is a party to the Council of Europe's data protection convention (Convention 108).

narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 and 13 October 2026 from the official gazette (BOPA) and government websites; a run cut off by a usage limit was resumed and its downloads re-read from the official texts. instruments.official_title: Codi sobre l'Ètica de la Intel·ligència Artificial d'Andorra
instruments.english_title: Andorran Code on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Government of Andorra (Secretariat of State for Digital Transformation and Telecommunications)
instruments.current_status: Approved by the Government and announced on the Andorra Digital site on 2 May 2024 (document dated 'Maig 2024'); the announcement states adherence will be required of the public sector for certain processes and is voluntary for other actors. Decree 327/2024 (art. 9.2.j) tasks the Data Intelligence Agency with developing and implementing the code.
instruments.summary: A 52-page ethics code approved by the Government of Andorra setting values, principles and a framework for trustworthy AI across the AI life cycle, aligned with the UNESCO Recommendation, the Council of Europe AI convention work, the OECD AI principles and the EU ethics guidelines. It covers human rights by design, ESG criteria, digital rights and neurorights, and generative AI, and gives recommendations for three audiences: the public sector (e.g. training public employees), the private sector and citizens. Adherence is required of the public sector for certain processes and voluntary for others.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Andorra's main AI-specific policy instrument; the reference framework for AI use in the public sector.

instruments.official_title: Decret 327/2024, del 21-8-2024, de govern de dades i de creació de l’Agència d’Intel·ligència de la Dada
instruments.english_title: Decree 327/2024 of 21 August 2024 on data governance and creating the Data Intelligence Agency
instruments.current_status: In force: computed from the final provision ('entra en vigor l’endemà de ser publicat') and publication in BOPA núm. 95 of 28 August 2024.
instruments.summary: Creates the Data Intelligence Agency (AID) and regulates the data-governance model for interoperability and data reuse in the public sector. Article 9.2 gives the Agency AI functions: contributing to the deployment, monitoring and supervision of AI systems and AI governance, developing tools and benchmarks to assess AI models, supervising rules on general-purpose AI models and investigating infringements, supporting rules on prohibited practices and high-risk AI, implementing the AI ethics code and defining a national AI action plan based on the national digital transformation strategy.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding instrument of Andorra's national AI body.

instruments.official_title: Llei 29/2021, del 28 d’octubre, qualificada de protecció de dades personals
instruments.english_title: Qualified Law 29/2021 of 28 October on personal data protection
instruments.current_status: In force: computed from final provision four ('entra en vigor en el termini de sis mesos des de la seva publicació') and publication in BOPA núm. 119 of 17 November 2021. Amended by Llei 12/2024, del 15 de juliol (BOPA núm. 87, 2024), and implemented by regulations approved by Decree 391/2022.
instruments.summary: Andorra's GDPR-aligned data protection law, replacing the 2003 law, applying to public and private controllers and processors and supervised by the Andorran Data Protection Agency (APDA). Article 25 gives data subjects the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing, including profiling, that produce legal effects, with limited exceptions (contract, authorising law with safeguards, explicit consent) and restrictions on special-category data. Controllers must inform data subjects of automated decision-making and the logic involved.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Governs personal data used to train and run AI systems and sets the automated decision-making safeguards.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl: BOPA PDF (44 pages) read via pdftotext; BOPA núm. 119, 17 November 2021; art. 25 and final provision four checked.

instruments.official_title: Llei 18/2026, del 15 de juliol, qualificada del Codi penal
instruments.english_title: Qualified Law 18/2026 of 15 July on the Criminal Code
instruments.current_status: Adopted 15 July 2026 and published in BOPA núm. 92 of 13 August 2026; not yet in force. Effective date computed from final provision five: in force four months after publication in the BOPA (six months for final provision two, one year for the corporate criminal liability provisions). Replaces the Llei 9/2005 Criminal Code.
instruments.summary: Andorra's new Criminal Code. Article 166 (non-consensual dissemination of intimate or manipulated material) punishes with three months to three years' imprisonment anyone who produces, manipulates or alters images or videos with AI technologies or synthetic-creation systems to make it appear that a person is engaged in sexually explicit acts or nude, and then disseminates them without consent. Penalties are aggravated when the victim is a minor, a current or former partner, or where the offender abuses a position of authority.
